messages.subject: YRe: looking to contract somebody to help stand up a R web app
parts:
You might also look at OpenCPU ... there's a bit more infrastructure on top of rApache

On Monday, August 27, 2012, Daróczi Gergely <ger...@snowl.net> wrote:
> Dear Markus,
> we are currently working on a web application (building on RApache) which is likely to be useful in your case.
> The webapp would deal with the back-end (storing data in DB, handling users and permissions, loading required packages, an editor to create statistical templates, rendering R output in HTML/pdf/docx format etc.), so users can concentrate solely on R and the output is automatically rendered in an IMHO pretty way.
> We are using some of our quite new packages building on Pandoc's markdown, so by visiting our project pages, you might get an insight how you can run R code in our forthcoming application and also how the R output would be rendered:
>
> pander is a wrapper around Pandoc and also provides a modified version of `brew` (I am pretty sure all list member know about this latter) which renders R objects in markdown with the option to export all those to HTML/docx/odt/pdf etc. including all the generated plots
> and rapport building on `pander` provides a way to create statistical templates to be run against any user specified data with optional parameters
>
> If you are interested in this project (estimated start: in the middle of September), please visit our signup page at rapporter.net.
> Do not be deterred by the minimal description crowded with some marketing slogans, users will definitely have the option to create custom templates (running any R code) with a fool-proof GUI to let even non useRs also enjoy your algorithms and the results :)
> I hope you would find that service (and my current message) useful, I could provide some public demos of the application on demand.
> Best,
> Gergely
>
> On Mon, Aug 27, 2012 at 10:29 PM, Markus <mark...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> About a year ago, I spent some time learning how to setup rapache with the goal building a R web app that would essentially allow users to upload data, use a package I wrote in R to analyze the data, and provide a PDF report output.  I am good with R and can usually hack through building a web page, but putting together a working R web app felt like it was over my head.  I got a version of rapache to work on a linux machine and feed it simple server requests, but was completely lost when it came connecting a proper front end.
>> I am about to retackle the project and am willing to throw some money at getting it initially setup this time around.
>> I'm thinking I want a rapache webserver setup on Amazon (or some other cloud location) with my package installed and connected to a Sencha (or similar) front end.  I think once the app is setup and working at a simple level, I will be able to work on updating and improving the front end and R code as necessary.
>> Looking for any suggestions on who to talk to and how much something like this might cost.  Also, should I be looking at the Revolution Analytics Web Services API?  Is that possibly a simpler solution for me?
>> Thanks,
>> Markus
>>
